data.name: Rishit
data.gender_notes: Rishit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from two words - 'Rishi' (sage) and 'it' (one who has mastered), Rishit signifies a person who has mastered his senses. The name Rishit carries the meaning “Lord of the senses” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Rishit usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the senses and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Rishit belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the senses.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rishit total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, a Rishi is considered a wise and knowledgeable person, a spiritual teacher and guide. The name Rishit, therefore, carries the meaning of a wise and enlightened individual, someone who embodies the qualities of a sage and inspires spiritually and intellectually.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rishit holds deep spiritual significance and carries an important message of self-discipline and self-mastery. It encourages one to control their senses and desires and strive towards the path of enlightenment and spiritual growth. In essence, it reminds us of the importance of living a virtuous and disciplined life in order to attain inner peace and outer success.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rishit is a name of divine wisdom and enlightenment. It symbolizes one's connection to the inner sage, the Rishi within, who guides towards truth and knowledge. A beacon of light in the spiritual journey, Rishit represents understanding and insight.

historical_references.reference: Rishi Rishyasringa was a renowned sage and the son of the sage Jatayu and the Vibhouti, a celestial nymph. He is considered as the youngest brother of the Pandava brothers. He played a significant role in the Mahabharata war, persuading Bhishma Pitamaha to lay down his arms before Arjuna.

Rishi Rishi is also mentioned in the Puranas as a sage who performed severe penance to gain the blessings of Lord Shiva. He is said to have meditated on Lord Shiva in the form of a Lingam, and his devotion was rewarded with the gift of a divine chariot known as Pushpaka Vimana.
